verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes the SK6812 addressable chain on GPIO13 as the software-controlled charge-status output.
Immediate context resolves the referenced LED as SK6812 Mini-E, and the client specifies its intended 3.3V supply.
The cited 3.7–5.5V operating range materially conflicts with the client-confirmed 3.3V LED supply.
The client specifies GPIO-controlled disconnection of the 5V LED rail to eliminate standby current.
The client selects the power-board 5V supply and requires logic-level shifting for the LED data line.
The explicit 5V and level-shifter decision resolves the earlier supply-voltage conflict.
The client changes the executable 5V-enable control assignment from GPIO3 to GPIO5.
The client confirms that the main PCB provides a JST electrical interconnect to the external LEDs.
The LED operating voltage and resulting need for a data-level shifter remain materially unresolved.
The client selects 5V operation and the specified 74AHCT1G125 data-level shifter based on the electrical thresholds.
The definitive 5V and level-shifter selection resolves the preceding electrical-interface ambiguity.
The exact LED part and package remain unresolved, materially affecting the documented PCB footprint and interface.
The client changes the PCB power-control behavior so LED power is switched independently from sensor power.
The client selects the exact OPSCO SK6812MINI-E part, LCSC C5149201, for the PCB design.
The client changes the LED rail to 3.3V, specifies direct ESP32 data drive, accepts the below-datasheet operating constraint, and validly removes the previously established level-shifter part.
The source gives a general board-placement preference and does not specifically entail placement of the LED connector; a board-layout Requirement is the better target.
The integrated-PCB architecture changes the LED-interface context and makes the prior main-board-specific interconnect attribute stale; pricing and milestone content are not encoded.
The source approves flexible connector placement but does not establish the proposed JST LED-interconnect value; the observation belongs to integrated-board connector layout.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The LEDs are now powered from 3.3V instead of 5V. At 3.3V supply the SK6812 data threshold drops to 2.31V, which the ESP32 3.3V output satisfies directly, so no level shifter is needed. The tradeoff is that 3.3V is slightly below the SK6812 datasheet minimum (3.7V), but it works reliably at indicator brightness levels.
